PAGE 1: Reading the clock
READING THE CLOCK
====

A clock helps us know what time it is. An analogue clock has a round face with the numbers 1 to 12, and two hands. The short hand is the hour hand. It tells us the hour. The long hand is the minute hand. It tells us the minutes.

When the minute hand points straight up at 12, it is exactly on the hour. We say the time is o'clock. When the hour hand points at 3 and the minute hand points at 12, the time is 3 o'clock.

When the minute hand points straight down at 6, half an hour has passed. We say it is half past. If the hour hand is between 6 and 7 and the minute hand is at 6, the time is half past 6, or 6:30.

### Digital time
A digital clock shows time with numbers. The first number is the hour and the second number is the minutes, for example 6:30. The two dots separate the hours from the minutes.

### Hours and minutes
There are 60 minutes in one hour. The minute hand takes one hour to go once round the clock face.

PAGE 2: Minutes past and minutes to the hour
MINUTES PAST AND MINUTES TO THE HOUR
====

The clock face has 12 numbers, and each number stands for 5 minutes. When the minute hand is on 1, five minutes have passed. On 2, ten minutes. On 3, fifteen minutes, and so on. On 12 it is 0 or 60 minutes.

To count minutes, count in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60.

### Minutes past
When the minute hand is on the right side of the clock (between 12 and 6), we say minutes past the hour. If the minute hand is on 4, that is 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past. With the hour hand just after 4, the time is 20 minutes past 4, or 4:20.

### Minutes to
When the minute hand is on the left side (between 6 and 12), we say minutes to the next hour. If it is on 9, the time is 15 minutes to the next hour, which is a quarter to. With the hour hand nearly at 8, the time is a quarter to 8, or 7:45.

### Quarter past and quarter to
• Quarter past means 15 minutes past the hour (minute hand on 3).
• Quarter to means 15 minutes before the next hour (minute hand on 9).

### Try it
What time is it when the minute hand is on 7 and the hour hand is between 2 and 3, past the halfway point? 7 × 5 = 35 minutes past 2, which is 2:35. We can also say 25 minutes to 3.

PAGE 3: a.m. and p.m.
A.M. AND P.M.
====

A day and a night together make 24 hours. The clock face only shows 12 hours, so each time on the clock happens twice in a day: once in the morning and once in the afternoon or evening. To tell the two apart, we add a.m. or p.m.

• a.m. is used from midnight (12 o'clock at night) until noon (12 o'clock midday). This is the time in the morning.
• p.m. is used from noon until midnight. This is the afternoon, evening and night.

====

Stand a stick in the ground in a sunny place. Every hour, mark the tip of its shadow with a small stone and measure the length. Write down the times and lengths. You will find the shadow is longest early and late in the day and shortest around midday.

If a tree's shadow is very short, the time is close to midday. If it is long and points to your right when you face north, it may be late afternoon. A shadow clock gives only a rough estimate, and it does not work at night or when clouds cover the Sun.

3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.

### Minutes to hours: divide by 60
150 minutes: 150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30. So 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes.

### Days to hours: multiply by 24
2 days = 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

### Hours to days: divide by 24
72 hours: 72 ÷ 24 = 3 days.

### Weeks to days: multiply by 7
3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days.

### Days to weeks: divide by 7
35 days: 35 ÷ 7 = 5 weeks. 17 days: 17 ÷ 7 = 2 remainder 3, so 17 days = 2 weeks and 3 days.

### Example
A school trip lasts 2 days. How many hours is that? 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

PAGE 6: Time duration
TIME DURATION
====

Duration is how long an event lasts. It is the time between the start and the end. To find the duration, count from the start time to the end time.

A maths lesson starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m. How long is the lesson?
Step 1: From 8:15 to 10:15 is 2 hours.
Step 2: From 10:15 to 10:40 is 25 minutes.
Step 3: Add: 2 hours + 25 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes.

MATHEMATICS — TIME · ANSWERS
====

1. B
   The minute hand at 6 means half past. The hour hand between 6 and 7 means it is after 6, so the time is 6:30.

2. C
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.

3. C
   1 day = 24 hours, so 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

4. B
   Afternoon times after noon use p.m., so it is 3:15 p.m.

5. B
   At midday the Sun is highest in the sky, so shadows are very short.

6. 2 hours 25 minutes
   8:15 to 10:15 is 2 hours (1 mark). 10:15 to 10:40 is 25 minutes (1 mark). Total 2 hours 25 minutes (1 mark).

7. 4 hours 15 minutes
   45 + 30 = 75 minutes and 2 + 1 = 3 hours (1 mark). 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes (1 mark). 3 h + 1 h 15 min = 4 h 15 min (1 mark).

8. 2 hours 45 minutes
   Change 5 h 20 min to 4 h 80 min (1 mark). 80 − 35 = 45 minutes (1 mark). 4 − 2 = 2 hours, giving 2 h 45 min (1 mark).

9. 6:00 p.m.
   4:20 + 1 hour = 5:20 p.m. (1 mark). 5:20 + 40 minutes = 6:00 p.m. (1 mark).

10. 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. 35 days = 5 weeks.
   150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30 (1 mark for 2 hours 30 minutes). 35 ÷ 7 = 5 (1 mark for 5 weeks). 1 mark for showing the division steps.

studyPages.body:
READING THE CLOCK
====

A clock helps us know what time it is. An analogue clock has a round face with the numbers 1 to 12, and two hands. The short hand is the hour hand. It tells us the hour. The long hand is the minute hand. It tells us the minutes.

When the minute hand points straight up at 12, it is exactly on the hour. We say the time is o'clock. When the hour hand points at 3 and the minute hand points at 12, the time is 3 o'clock.

When the minute hand points straight down at 6, half an hour has passed. We say it is half past. If the hour hand is between 6 and 7 and the minute hand is at 6, the time is half past 6, or 6:30.

### Digital time
A digital clock shows time with numbers. The first number is the hour and the second number is the minutes, for example 6:30. The two dots separate the hours from the minutes.

### Hours and minutes
There are 60 minutes in one hour. The minute hand takes one hour to go once round the clock face.

studyPages.title: Minutes past and minutes to the hour
studyPages.body:
MINUTES PAST AND MINUTES TO THE HOUR
====

The clock face has 12 numbers, and each number stands for 5 minutes. When the minute hand is on 1, five minutes have passed. On 2, ten minutes. On 3, fifteen minutes, and so on. On 12 it is 0 or 60 minutes.

To count minutes, count in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60.

### Minutes past
When the minute hand is on the right side of the clock (between 12 and 6), we say minutes past the hour. If the minute hand is on 4, that is 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past. With the hour hand just after 4, the time is 20 minutes past 4, or 4:20.

### Minutes to
When the minute hand is on the left side (between 6 and 12), we say minutes to the next hour. If it is on 9, the time is 15 minutes to the next hour, which is a quarter to. With the hour hand nearly at 8, the time is a quarter to 8, or 7:45.

### Quarter past and quarter to
• Quarter past means 15 minutes past the hour (minute hand on 3).
• Quarter to means 15 minutes before the next hour (minute hand on 9).

### Try it
What time is it when the minute hand is on 7 and the hour hand is between 2 and 3, past the halfway point? 7 × 5 = 35 minutes past 2, which is 2:35. We can also say 25 minutes to 3.

studyPages.title: a.m. and p.m.
studyPages.body:
A.M. AND P.M.
====

A day and a night together make 24 hours. The clock face only shows 12 hours, so each time on the clock happens twice in a day: once in the morning and once in the afternoon or evening. To tell the two apart, we add a.m. or p.m.

• a.m. is used from midnight (12 o'clock at night) until noon (12 o'clock midday). This is the time in the morning.
• p.m. is used from noon until midnight. This is the afternoon, evening and night.

• Waking up at 6:30: 6:30 a.m.
• Lunch at 1:00: 1:00 p.m.
• Going to bed at 9:00: 9:00 p.m.
• A cockerel crows at dawn: about 5:00 a.m.

### Estimating time of day
Think about what you are doing and whether it is light or dark. Sunrise is around 6 in the morning and sunset is around 6 in the evening in most parts of Kenya, because Kenya lies close to the equator.

studyPages.title: Estimating time using shadows
studyPages.body:
ESTIMATING TIME USING SHADOWS
====

Before clocks, people used the Sun to estimate the time of day. When the Sun shines on a tree or a building, it makes a shadow on the ground. The length of the shadow changes during the day.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 4: Shadows of a post in the morning, midday and afternoon
ALT: A post with a long shadow on the right in the morning when the Sun is low on the left, a very short shadow at midday when the Sun is overhead, and a long shadow on the left in the afternoon when the Sun is low on the right
PAYLOAD:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 420 165" width="420" height="165" role="img">
<line x1="10" y1="130" x2="410" y2="130" stroke="#795548" stroke-width="3"/>
<line x1="60" y1="130" x2="60" y2="80" stroke="#111" stroke-width="5"/><line x1="60" y1="130" x2="150" y2="130" stroke="#424242" stroke-width="6"/><circle cx="20" cy="22" r="10" fill="#ffca28" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="20" y1="22" x2="60" y2="80" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><text x="105" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#111">Morning</text><line x1="210" y1="130" x2="210" y2="80" stroke="#111" stroke-width="5"/><line x1="210" y1="130" x2="218" y2="130" stroke="#424242" stroke-width="6"/><circle cx="210" cy="12" r="10" fill="#ffca28" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="210" y1="12" x2="210" y2="80" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><text x="214" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#111">Midday</text><line x1="350" y1="130" x2="350" y2="80" stroke="#111" stroke-width="5"/><line x1="350" y1="130" x2="270" y2="130" stroke="#424242" stroke-width="6"/><circle cx="395" cy="22" r="10" fill="#ffca28" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="395" y1="22" x2="350" y2="80" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><text x="310" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#111">Afternoon</text>
</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 4: Shadows of a post in the morning, midday and afternoon
[/DIAGRAM]
• In the early morning the Sun is low in the east. Shadows are long and point towards the west.
• As the morning goes on, shadows become shorter.
• At midday the Sun is high in the sky. Shadows are very short.
• In the afternoon the Sun moves towards the west. Shadows get longer again and point towards the east.

### An experiment
Stand a stick in the ground in a sunny place. Every hour, mark the tip of its shadow with a small stone and measure the length. Write down the times and lengths. You will find the shadow is longest early and late in the day and shortest around midday.

### What can we say?
If a tree's shadow is very short, the time is close to midday. If it is long and points to your right when you face north, it may be late afternoon. A shadow clock gives only a rough estimate, and it does not work at night or when clouds cover the Sun.

====

### Hours to minutes: multiply by 60
3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.

### Minutes to hours: divide by 60
150 minutes: 150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30. So 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes.

### Days to hours: multiply by 24
2 days = 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

### Hours to days: divide by 24
72 hours: 72 ÷ 24 = 3 days.

### Weeks to days: multiply by 7
3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days.

### Days to weeks: divide by 7
35 days: 35 ÷ 7 = 5 weeks. 17 days: 17 ÷ 7 = 2 remainder 3, so 17 days = 2 weeks and 3 days.

### Example
A school trip lasts 2 days. How many hours is that? 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

studyPages.title: Time duration
studyPages.body:
TIME DURATION
====

Duration is how long an event lasts. It is the time between the start and the end. To find the duration, count from the start time to the end time.

A maths lesson starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m. How long is the lesson?
Step 1: From 8:15 to 10:15 is 2 hours.
Step 2: From 10:15 to 10:40 is 25 minutes.
Step 3: Add: 2 hours + 25 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes.

### Crossing noon
A bus leaves at 10:30 a.m. and arrives at 2:15 p.m. From 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. is 2 hours. From 12:30 to 2:15 p.m. is 1 hour 45 minutes. Total = 3 hours 45 minutes.

### Finding the end time
A film starts at 4:20 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 40 minutes. Add 1 hour: 5:20 p.m. Add 40 minutes: 6:00 p.m. The film ends at 6:00 p.m.

### Reading start and end
Always check whether the times are a.m. or p.m. before working out the duration.

studyPages.body:
ADDING AND SUBTRACTING TIME
====

We can add and subtract quantities of time given in hours and minutes. Add or subtract the minutes, then the hours. If the minutes reach 60 or more, change 60 minutes into 1 hour.

Step 1: Add the minutes: 45 + 30 = 75 minutes.
Step 2: Add the hours: 2 + 1 = 3 hours.
Step 3: 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes, so 3 hours 75 minutes = 4 hours 15 minutes.

### Subtraction
Subtract 2 hours 35 minutes from 5 hours 20 minutes.
Step 1: 20 minutes is smaller than 35 minutes, so change 1 hour into 60 minutes. 5 hours 20 minutes becomes 4 hours 80 minutes.
Step 2: Subtract the minutes: 80 − 35 = 45 minutes.
Step 3: Subtract the hours: 4 − 2 = 2 hours.
The answer is 2 hours 45 minutes.

### Check by adding
2 h 45 min + 2 h 35 min = 4 h 80 min = 5 h 20 min. It matches.

### Example
Wanjiru studied for 1 hour 20 minutes on Monday and 45 minutes on Tuesday. Total = 1 h 20 min + 45 min = 1 h 65 min = 2 h 5 min.

### How to record
Step 1: Write down the start time using a.m. or p.m.
Step 2: Write the end time.
Step 3: Work out the duration by counting on from the start.
Step 4: Write the duration in hours and minutes.

### Try it
Time how long it takes to walk to school, eat lunch and read a story. Use a clock or a watch. Record your results in a table like the one above.

### Summary
• The hour hand is short and the minute hand is long.
• Each number on the clock face stands for 5 minutes.
• a.m. is from midnight to noon. p.m. is from noon to midnight.
• 1 hour = 60 minutes, 1 day = 24 hours and 1 week = 7 days.
• Duration is the time between the start and the end of an event.
